about.title: About PhishGuard AI
about.description: PhishGuard AI is a web-based cybersecurity platform developed as a master's thesis project in Computer Systems and Technologies. It combines a React interface, an Express API, detection services, and a MySQL database for storing analysis results.
about.phishingText: The phishing module evaluates sender email, suspicious URLs, message text, domain mismatch, shorteners, urgency terms, and dangerous keywords.
about.imageText: The image module accepts validated uploads, uses a pretrained classifier when available, and combines model output with file-level signals.
about.modelPathText: The service layer can be extended with text classification, URL reputation APIs, image forensics models, and confidence calibration.
about.databaseText: Analysis records are designed around normalized MySQL tables for checks, detection results, users, and audit logs.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.description: Common questions about PhishGuard AI analysis, storage, accuracy, and dashboard access.

items.question: How does phishing detection work?
items.answer: The phishing module uses backend rules to evaluate sender domains, suspicious URLs, urgency language, Bulgarian scam phrases, sensitive data requests, and domain mismatch.

items.question: How are AI-generated images analyzed?
items.answer: Uploaded images are validated and analyzed through the image detection module. When the model service is running, PhishGuard AI uses a pretrained HuggingFace classifier to estimate the probability that an image is AI-generated. The final result combines the model prediction with metadata and forensic signals such as EXIF presence, software tags, dimensions, format and compression indicators.

items.question: Is my uploaded data stored?
items.answer: The platform stores analysis records and file metadata for dashboard history. Access is scoped by user role.

items.question: Can I delete my history?
items.answer: Yes. Logged-in users can delete their own scan history from the Dashboard using Clear History. The action affects only the current user's phishing and image scan records. Administrative audit records may be preserved for security and abuse prevention.

items.question: How accurate is the detection system?
items.answer: Detection is probabilistic and should not be treated as absolute proof. High-risk results should still be reviewed by a human analyst.

items.question: Who can access dashboard data?
items.answer: Regular users can access only their own records. Admin users can review global checks and logs through the admin panel.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.description: How PhishGuard AI handles accounts, scan history, uploaded files, authentication data, and user rights.

sections.title: Account Data
sections.text: We store account information required for login, role-based access, and dashboard ownership. Passwords are stored as hashes and are never displayed by the application.

sections.title: Scan History
sections.text: Phishing and image checks are stored so users can review previous results. Regular users can access only their own records, while administrators can review platform-wide records.

sections.title: Image Uploads
sections.text: Uploaded images are processed for validation and analysis metadata. The workflow stores file information and analysis results, not a public gallery.

sections.title: Authentication And Sessions
sections.text: The frontend stores an authentication token locally so users can access protected pages. Users should sign out on shared devices.

sections.title: User Rights
sections.text: Users may request account review, correction of inaccurate data, or removal of stored analysis records.

sections.title: Security Practices
sections.text: The platform uses authentication, role checks, password hashing, and audit logs to reduce unauthorized access risk.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.description: Rules for using PhishGuard AI as a security analysis and academic demonstration platform.

sections.title: Acceptable Use
sections.text: Users may analyze suspicious messages and image files for educational, research, and defensive security purposes.

sections.title: Prohibited Use
sections.text: The platform must not be used to create phishing campaigns, harass users, upload harmful content, or attempt unauthorized access.

sections.title: Analysis Limitations
sections.text: Results are indicators, not final legal or forensic conclusions. High-impact decisions require additional tools and expert review.

sections.title: Moderation Rights
sections.text: Administrators may suspend or ban accounts that abuse the system, bypass controls, or submit harmful content.

sections.title: Liability
sections.text: PhishGuard AI is a thesis project and should be treated as a research implementation rather than a commercial security guarantee.

cookies.title: Cookie Policy
cookies.description: How local storage and browser-based preferences are used by PhishGuard AI.

sections.title: Authentication Storage
sections.text: The application stores an authentication token locally after login so protected API requests can be made from the browser.

sections.title: Cookie Consent Choice
sections.text: The cookie banner stores whether a user accepted or declined the notice so it does not appear on every page load.

sections.title: Security And Preferences
sections.text: Browser storage is used only for session continuity and interface preferences in the current implementation.

sections.title: Managing Storage
sections.text: Users can clear browser storage at any time. Doing so removes the local login state and cookie preference.

security.title: Security Policy
security.description: Security practices, account protections, and responsible disclosure guidance for PhishGuard AI.

sections.title: Account Security
sections.text: Users should choose strong passwords and sign out on shared machines. Administrative features are protected by role-based middleware.

sections.title: Password Handling
sections.text: Passwords are hashed before storage. The application never needs to read or display a plain user password.

sections.title: JWT Authentication
sections.text: Protected API requests require a valid token. Dashboard and admin data are filtered by authenticated user and role.

sections.title: Data Protection
sections.text: Analysis results are stored with ownership metadata so regular users see only their own history.

sections.title: Detection Limitations
sections.text: Phishing and image analysis results are security signals and do not replace professional incident response or forensic review.

sections.title: Responsible Disclosure
sections.text: Security issues should be reported through the contact page with clear reproduction steps and affected components.
